findings.title: Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the 4-arg `(max_width, max_height)` version
findings.body: Ruby has no method overloading, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined just above it. Existing callers that pass width and height (e.g. post-processing or avatar downsizing) now bind `max_height` to `opts` and pass a bare width as `dimensions`. `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` then runs on an Integer and raises a TypeError, or the `-resize` arguments come out wrong. Use a distinct method name, or detect a string dimension argument inside a single method.

findings.title: Percentage resize fails for animated GIFs (gifsicle) and failures are ignored
findings.body: When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is on and the file is a GIF, `downsize` goes through `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle does not accept percentage geometry, so the command fails. The loop ignores the boolean result of `OptimizedImage.downsize` and just repeats the same failing call up to 5 times. The oversized file then goes to `Upload.create_for` and is rejected anyway. Large animated GIFs are never downsized, and CPU is wasted on futile shell-outs. Check the return value and break on failure, and build an absolute size for gifsicle.

findings.title: Loop relies on `tempfile.size` of the open descriptor after an external in-place rewrite
findings.body: The file is rewritten in place by an external `convert` and then by ImageOptim, which may write a new file and rename it over the path. `tempfile.size` stats the already-open descriptor, so it can keep reporting the old inode's size. The loop would then keep shrinking needlessly, and the size passed to `Upload.create_for` would be stale. Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` instead.

findings.title: Client size check hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb
findings.body: The client limit used to come from `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb`; it is now 10MB for every type. Downsizing only applies to images, so attachments larger than the configured `max_attachment_size_kb` now pass client validation and fail on the server after the whole upload. Sites that configured a limit above 10MB can no longer upload files they are allowed to upload. The error text also reports 10MB, not the real attachment limit. Keep using the site setting for attachments.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB download limit for API URL uploads
findings.body: The download limit is now a hardcoded `10.megabytes` for every upload type. For attachments this no longer matches `max_attachment_size_kb`: sites configured above 10MB can't import larger files via URL. Files above the limit are downloaded unnecessarily before being rejected. The 10MB magic number is also duplicated across client and server instead of coming from a setting.

findings.title: No tests for automatic downsizing or the new `downsize` signature
findings.body: The new downsize loop and the changed `OptimizedImage.downsize` / `optimize` signatures have no specs. A spec exercising the existing `(max_width, max_height)` callers would have caught the method being overwritten.
